SWE-bench Verified.note: Fixes bugs from GitHub issues and runs unit tests. Leading scores have converged, and many tasks have entered training data.

DeepSWE.name: DeepSWE
DeepSWE.note: A fixed controlled system with harder, longer tasks. Retained as a cross-reference from v16.

FrontierCode.name: FrontierCode
FrontierCode.note: Open-source maintainers write tasks and judge whether they would merge the PR. The primary coding benchmark from v16.

reasoning.blurb: Mathematics, logic and unfamiliar rules: can the model reason through new problems?

vision.blurb: Image-comprehension evidence remains in the overall board. Understanding images and designing attractive work are different abilities.

multilingual.name: Chinese and multilingual
multilingual.blurb: Complementary language evidence. English writing performance does not establish Chinese capability.

artificial-analysis.name: AA Index
artificial-analysis.description: Reruns multiple current benchmarks in one environment to produce an overall capability score. Prices are reference information and do not affect the score.
artificial-analysis.what: Use only the official Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. Performance and price fields from the API do not count toward ranking.
artificial-analysis.usage: Broad task evidence receives 30%. The 10 underlying benchmarks in v4.3 have been checked for duplicate votes with active specialized benchmarks. Keep the index intact; do not present an aggregate as an individual result.
artificial-analysis.limits: Without an API key, this entire source is excluded for the round; no 50-point substitute is assigned. Web scraping must not replace the API. Display requires attribution and the index version.
artificial-analysis.license: API data displayed or shared must carry prominent attribution. Redistribution rights and custom terms require separate agreement and compliance with the Terms of Use.

livebench-general.name: LiveBench
livebench-general.description: Continuously refreshed tasks with automatically verifiable answers test whether models hold up when the questions change.
livebench-general.what: Keep the official Global Average as an overall cross-reference. Ranking uses nonoverlapping specialized tasks.
livebench-general.usage: The raw Global Average remains a cross-reference. Ranking votes come from nonoverlapping specialized tasks.
livebench-general.limits: An overall average can dilute changes in specific capabilities. It is a cross-reference and adds no duplicate votes. Participating organization Abacus.AI also develops Smaug; results exclusive to its models need support from other independent sources.

arena-text.name: Arena Text
arena-text.description: People compare anonymous pairs of answers and choose which they prefer to read, adding overall experience that multiple-choice tests miss.
arena-text.what: Use only the Text Overall style-controlled main board in official published snapshots. Do not scrape the live arena.ai page.
arena-text.usage: The 10% human-preference budget is split into 5% overall text and 5% creative writing. Arena coding and vision tasks still share the same evidence family. Freshness follows the official score data timestamp.
arena-text.limits: Human preference depends on style, user demographics and prompt distribution. Overall and creative categories have overlapping votes and share the original human-preference budget. They do not count as two independent organizations.

arena-webdev.name: Arena WebDev
arena-webdev.description: Human blind preference tests whether websites are usable and ready to deliver.
arena-webdev.what: Use only the WebDev overall board in official published snapshots. Do not scrape the live arena.ai page. Together with Text, it forms one Arena family vote.
arena-webdev.usage: Receives 2.4% from the coding and design budget. In the aesthetics category it measures preference for websites, not code accuracy. It still shares the evidence family with other Arena tasks.
arena-webdev.limits: Its preference construct is correlated with Text.

livebench-writing.name: LiveBench · Language and instruction following
livebench-writing.description: Average of Language + IF, weighted 50% each.
livebench-writing.what: Compute Language and IF category scores separately, average them with 50% weight each, then round to one decimal. This two-category average differs from selecting a single category on the official site. Language measures language comprehension; IF measures instruction and format constraints. Neither establishes fiction writing quality.
livebench-writing.usage: Retains 3% of the overall writing and expression budget. Excluded from the literary creative-writing category.
livebench-writing.limits: The two-category average measures combined performance, not Language alone. Switching categories or including fine-tuned models on the official page changes scores and ranks. Participating organization Abacus.AI also develops Smaug; results exclusive to its models need support from other independent sources.
livebench-writing.attribution: LiveBench publishes the component scores. {{siteName}} averages the two categories above with equal weight and ranks the results. The two-category average and the {{siteName}} consensus index use different scales and cannot be added directly.

components.note: Language + IF are weighted 50% each, using unrounded component scores for the average.
components.label: Two-category average

arena-creative-writing.name: Arena · Creative writing blind preference
arena-creative-writing.description: People choose between anonymous stories, poems and other creative writing to assess whether the work engages readers.
arena-creative-writing.what: Read the creative_writing category in the official text_style_control dataset, using style-controlled Bradley–Terry scores and confidence intervals. Do not substitute overall text or professional-writing scores.
arena-creative-writing.usage: Counts toward ranking. Receives 5% from the original 10% human-preference budget; overall text keeps 5%, with no increase in total budget. Shares the evidence family with other Arena tasks.
arena-creative-writing.limits: Open user prompts are classified automatically; they are not all long-form fiction or Chinese creative writing. Votes include personal preferences. Overlap with Arena overall text and professional writing prevents it from counting as another independent organization.
arena-creative-writing.license: CC BY 4.0 · Official Arena Hugging Face leaderboard-dataset; retain attribution and source links and disclose aggregation changes.

design-arena-design.name: Design Arena · Visual design
design-arena-design.description: Human blind preference for website, interface, chart and slide designs.
design-arena-design.what: Compare only base models in Models Arena. Design tasks share a family budget. Subcategories are not independent sources and must not duplicate votes from the codecategories total.
design-arena-design.usage: Under observation: the formal API protocol and display terms are clear. Approved access and verification of individual raw results are pending. No collection or ranking yet.
design-arena-design.limits: The public website does not replace API authorization. Models, Agents and Builders must not be ranked together.
design-arena-design.license: Formal API data permits personal and commercial display with attribution and a visible official link. API access requires an approved application.

eq-emotional-v4.name: EQ-Bench 4 · Emotional and interpersonal understanding
eq-emotional-v4.description: Understanding emotions, implicit needs and different communication preferences in multi-turn conversations.
eq-emotional-v4.what: 120 simulated characters, 16 role-play turns and rotating blind judgments by three model judges. Use only Elo; behavioral traits are not capabilities where higher is always better. The older v3 adds no duplicate votes.
eq-emotional-v4.usage: Under observation: public data and licensing are available, but a new evaluation round is pending. Validity windows are not extended to meet category source counts.
eq-emotional-v4.limits: Simulated English conversations have not been validated by human experts. Results do not equal real user satisfaction or Chinese emotional intelligence. Current results exceed the 45-day window.
eq-emotional-v4.license: MIT · Metadata declaration in the EQ-bench-site README

lechmazur-short-story.name: Short-Story · Short fiction
lechmazur-short-story.description: Naturally incorporates specified characters, plot and style into a complete short story.
lechmazur-short-story.what: 600–800-word stories with 10 creative requirements, identical prompts, three judges and bidirectional comparisons. Use the main Thurstone score; BT is diagnostic only and adds no votes. Multiple tiers follow fixed selection rules.
lechmazur-short-story.usage: Under observation: integration awaits clear formal data reuse terms and resolution of differences between the README and machine-readable results.
lechmazur-short-story.limits: Model judges have literary preferences; some models have not completed every story. Short-story performance does not establish long-form fiction or Chinese writing quality.
lechmazur-short-story.license: No explicit leaderboard data reuse license found. A public GitHub repository does not imply open authorization.

tonebench-scripts.name: ToneBench · Style and scripts
tonebench-scripts.description: Writes video scripts in a specified author’s style, assessing openings, structure, expression and spoken pacing.
tonebench-scripts.what: 10 real script tasks, repeated generations and three judges. Compare only identical tasks, rubrics, judges and run fingerprints. Exclude rows with fallback to other models; do not choose configurations by each column’s highest score.
tonebench-scripts.usage: Under observation: data protocol and current coverage are good. Display terms and pure-model configurations still need verification.
tonebench-scripts.limits: Favors the style of one Towards AI channel; exact tasks and reference scripts are not public. The current first-place result includes Fable 5 + Opus 4.8 fallback and cannot represent a single model.
tonebench-scripts.license: Public JSON is readable, but explicit data aggregation and display terms have not been found.

tubelab-scriptwriting.name: TubeLab · Video scripts
tubelab-scriptwriting.description: Writes scripts for different video channels, comparing story organization, style, pacing and clarity.
tubelab-scriptwriting.what: A common TubeLab Scriptwriter, 12 tasks and 6 writing-quality criteria. Three model judges do not judge their own organization’s models; failed tasks retain penalties. Cost and speed do not affect capability scores.
tubelab-scriptwriting.usage: Under observation: stable raw data, accurate evaluation dates and reuse terms are pending. Display pages do not replace verifiable results.
tubelab-scriptwriting.limits: The Scriptwriter workflow affects models. OpenAI uses the lowest reasoning tier, so results cannot be generalized to other tiers. Spoken video scripts are not screenplays.
tubelab-scriptwriting.license: Stable result exports and public aggregation permission have not been confirmed.

ncbench-author-workflow.name: NC Bench · Author workflow
ncbench-author-workflow.description: Helps authors rewrite, continue, summarize, translate and organize creative ideas.
ncbench-author-workflow.what: Consider only pure quality scores for independent writing and text editing. Rank Score includes price, speed and reliability and is explicitly excluded.
ncbench-author-workflow.usage: Under observation: comparable raw task-level quality scores, actual update dates and display terms need verification.
ncbench-author-workflow.limits: The aggregate Rank Score mixes factors other than capability. Uneven task coverage prevents direct use of the homepage aggregate rank.
ncbench-author-workflow.license: Machine-readable results and data reuse terms have not been confirmed.

wordsmith-editing.name: Wordsmith · Manuscript editing
wordsmith-editing.description: Writes editorial notes, line edits and a final proofread for unpublished manuscripts.
wordsmith-editing.what: October 2026 pilot: 12 model configurations across craft notes, line edits and polish, scored 0–100 with 95% intervals. Judges from different model makers never grade their own maker's models.
wordsmith-editing.usage: Under observation, not scored: there is no data reuse license and no machine-readable results, and Wordsmith, which sells a manuscript editing product, writes and grades the test itself. Instructions, checklist and pages are unpublished, so results cannot be checked. Reassess once a license is stated, machine-readable results are published and the judges are validated against human editors.
wordsmith-editing.limits: Described by its operator as a pilot, not an independent certification. Small sample with wide intervals; judges not yet checked against human editors; English manuscripts only.
wordsmith-editing.license: No data license is stated on the page.

openvibeeval-design.name: OpenVibeEval · Web designs
openvibeeval-design.description: Compares websites, accessibility and blind preferences to assess design performance with different tools.
openvibeeval-design.what: Store model and harness separately. Accessibility scores are not aesthetics scores; independent blind preferences and identical run conditions must be verified before adoption.
openvibeeval-design.usage: Under observation: raw preference data from sufficient blind tests under matching conditions and publication dates are still needed.
openvibeeval-design.limits: Models use different tools. The main table measures accessibility and task outcomes, not a common aesthetics vote.
openvibeeval-design.license: Stable result exports and public aggregation permission have not been confirmed.

svgbench-arena.name: SVGBench · Vector graphics blind preference
svgbench-arena.description: Blind choices between SVGs from identical prompts assess visual clarity and graphical expression.
svgbench-arena.what: Require complete blind-test scores meeting prompt-coverage thresholds. Registered model counts are not valid ranked model counts. Share a related task family with other SVG benchmarks.
svgbench-arena.usage: Under observation: stable raw results, verifiable update times and display terms are pending.
svgbench-arena.limits: Website statistics do not prove that every new model has enough evaluations. Without raw tables and timestamps, coverage is not claimed.
svgbench-arena.license: No explicit result reuse license found.

rapidata-svg.name: Rapidata SVG
rapidata-svg.description: People compare model-generated vector graphics to evaluate visual preferences directly.
rapidata-svg.what: Use only Preference Elo for the same static SVG task. Alignment, Coherence and Overall add no duplicate votes. Use public score tables from a fixed official dataset version, traceable to original human comparisons.
rapidata-svg.usage: Under observation: official data and licensing are available, but three rolling DeepSeek aliases lack fixed-version evidence, so the entire score table is withheld. Awaiting run versions from the organization; active sources’ budgets have not been reduced.
rapidata-svg.limits: SVG drawing does not represent all interface design. Public raw data lacks model versions, generation dates and API fingerprints, so rolling API version changes cannot be established. A leaderboard update date cannot establish a model version.
rapidata-svg.license: CC BY 4.0 · Rapidata/svg-benchmark; retain official attribution and data links.

eq-creative.name: Creative Writing v3
eq-creative.what: The official CSV is embedded in a data script. Use Elo; Sonnet 4.6 judges wins. Style, repetition rate and rubric scores add no duplicate votes.
eq-creative.usage: Counts toward ranking; the two writing benchmarks share 6% in total. More tasks or models do not increase their weight.
eq-creative.limits: Primarily English writing, judged by models. The same judge and related tasks share a budget. Results do not represent Chinese writing quality.
eq-creative.license: MIT · Metadata declaration in the EQ-bench-site README

eq-longform.name: Longform Writing
eq-longform.description: Coherence and completeness of long-form stories
eq-longform.what: Use overall_score_100, assessing plot and expression across eight chapters. Judge preferences are disclosed as a limitation.
eq-longform.usage: Counts toward ranking; the two writing benchmarks share 6% in total. More tasks or models do not increase their weight.
eq-longform.limits: Primarily English writing, judged by models. The same judge and related tasks share a budget. Results do not represent Chinese writing quality.
eq-longform.license: MIT · Metadata declaration in the EQ-bench-site README

frontiercode.name: FrontierCode
frontiercode.description: Quality, tests and scope of changes in real repository tasks
frontiercode.what: Open-source maintainers write tasks asking whether they would merge the PR. Tests, rubrics and validators jointly score results; runs accessing sources containing answers receive zero. Uses the fixed v1.1 main set of 100 tasks.
frontiercode.usage: Receives 4.8% from the coding and design budget and is the primary coding benchmark from v16. Each model runs in its organization’s Agent (Codex, Claude Code, Devin, etc.), represented by its highest reasoning tier.
frontiercode.limits: Compares model + its own Agent systems, rather than bare models. Agent tools and prompts differ. With 100 tasks, differences between nearby ranks may fall within noise.
frontiercode.license: Cites structured results publicly released by Cognition, with attribution and a link to the original page. Results are withdrawn at the rights holder’s request.

deepswe-v1-1.name: DeepSWE v1.1
deepswe-v1-1.description: Edits repositories and fixes defects in a common coding-assistant environment to compare the coding models themselves.
deepswe-v1-1.what: Use only pass@1. Select a representative configuration within a common harness by predetermined reasoning-tier priority.
deepswe-v1-1.usage: Receives 1.2% from the coding and design budget. From v16, FrontierCode leads coding evidence; DeepSWE remains a cross-reference. Uses a fixed controlled system and version.
deepswe-v1-1.limits: Still measures a model + mini-swe-agent system. Major version changes require separate snapshots.
deepswe-v1-1.license: Official public structured results; private administrator observation only, with licensing reviewed before public display

taptap-maker.name: TapTap Maker
taptap-maker.description: Builds working features in Lua inside a real game engine. Scores come from engine execution, rather than another model’s judgment.
taptap-maker.what: Use only the official main_board L2 pass rate. Cost, speed, Held-out and category scores add no votes. Select one representative row per base model using fixed reasoning-tier priority, without considering scores.
taptap-maker.usage: Receives 2.4% from the coding and design budget, using a fixed engine and L2 metric.
taptap-maker.limits: One engine and one language do not generalize to other stacks. Models may use different agent drivers. The closed-source harness prevents task-by-task replication.
taptap-maker.license: Official public results; public display retains official attribution. Full redistribution authorization remains subject to Yiwan / TapTap terms.

livebench-coding.name: LiveBench · Coding average
livebench-coding.description: Average of Coding + Agentic Coding, weighted 50% each.
livebench-coding.what: Compute Coding and Agentic Coding category scores separately, average them with 50% weight each, then round to one decimal. This two-category average differs from selecting a single category on the official site.
livebench-coding.usage: The two-category average counts as one piece of ranking evidence. All specialized tasks share the LiveBench evidence family. Global Average is a cross-reference and adds no duplicate votes.
livebench-coding.limits: The two-category average measures combined performance, not Coding alone. Switching categories or including fine-tuned models on the official page changes scores and ranks. Participating organization Abacus.AI also develops Smaug; results exclusive to its models need support from other independent sources.
livebench-coding.attribution: LiveBench publishes the component scores. {{siteName}} averages the two categories above with equal weight and ranks the results. The two-category average and the {{siteName}} consensus index use different scales and cannot be added directly.

components.note: Coding + Agentic Coding are weighted 50% each, using unrounded component scores for the average.

hyper-tau.name: Hyper-τ-bench
hyper-tau.description: Builds and tests working customer-service agents from business documentation.
hyper-tau.what: Measures agent development and debugging, separately from direct customer service in τ³-Banking. Development tools, run duration and acceptance environment are fixed; do not choose the highest result across systems.
hyper-tau.usage: Under observation: could add coding and business-system development evidence. Raw results, licensing and fixed run conditions must be reviewed first. A new release does not automatically count toward ranking.
hyper-tau.limits: Under observation: could add coding and business-system development evidence. Raw results, licensing and fixed run conditions must be reviewed first. A new release does not automatically count toward ranking.
hyper-tau.license: Leaderboard data usage terms remain to be confirmed.

swe-rebench.name: SWE-rebench
swe-rebench.description: Continuously collects real repository issues to compare software repair across programming languages.
swe-rebench.what: Fix the task window, ReAct environment and text/tools protocol. Use average resolution rates and standard errors from repeated runs. Complete Agent products are not treated as base models.
swe-rebench.usage: Candidate under observation: real repository tasks could add useful evidence. Verifiable run dates, a stable score protocol and display terms are pending. Automated collection and ranking are not enabled.
swe-rebench.limits: Rolling tasks, runtime environment and task windows affect comparability. Recent website maintenance does not mean all models were retested.
swe-rebench.license: The official Hugging Face CC BY 4.0 dataset contains tasks. Stable exports and display terms for final website scores remain unconfirmed.

lhtb.name: LHTB
lhtb.description: Sustained terminal use to complete complex engineering and tool tasks over longer periods.
lhtb.what: Compare 90-minute, 2-hour and 3-hour budgets separately. Judging protocols before and after fixes cannot be ranked together. The best results from different Agents are not common model scores.
lhtb.usage: Candidate under observation: awaiting new batches explicitly identifying the fixed protocol. Existing old scores are not automatically collected into public boards or ranked. This does not claim every old result exploited a flaw.
lhtb.limits: The organization disclosed judging-information leakage. Current evidence does not establish that existing scores use the same isolated judging protocol. Task-source overlap with other professional benchmarks needs review.
lhtb.license: Apache 2.0 · Official IntelligenceLab/LHTB-leaderboard results dataset; retain attribution and change notes.

terminal-bench-4.name: Terminal-Bench 4
terminal-bench-4.description: Retains raw terminal-task scores for models paired with different Agents for cross-checking.
terminal-bench-4.what: Fix Terminal-Bench 4.0 and retain model, Agent version, reasoning tier and run count separately. Different tool systems do not represent common model conditions.
terminal-bench-4.usage: Raw results for reference: automatically collected after locking the official submission list and data version. Retain each system configuration without selecting a representative model score. Cross-checks only; excluded from overall and coding ranks.
terminal-bench-4.limits: Models use different tools such as Claude Code, Codex, GrokBuild and mini-SWE. AA v4.3 already includes Terminal-Bench v4, so it must not add overall vote weight again.
terminal-bench-4.license: Apache 2.0 · Official result submissions in harbor-framework/terminal-bench; retain attribution, protocol and change notes.

epoch-mirrorcode.limits: For reference only; excluded from overall and category scores.

configurationLabels.unreported: Reasoning tier not reported by the source

selectionReasons.firstParty: Uses the highest available first-party reasoning tier at this source, following predetermined rules. Selection does not consider scores.
selectionReasons.sourceDefault: This source does not distinguish reasoning tiers, so its official default configuration is used.
selectionReasons.lowerPriority: This configuration is retained for verification, but its fixed priority is below the representative configuration for this metric.
selectionReasons.scaffoldedSelected: This source uses the same controlled system for all models. Selection follows predetermined reasoning-tier priority, retains configuration details and attributes the score to the base model.
selectionReasons.scaffoldedLower: This configuration is retained for verification, but its fixed priority is below the system configuration selected for this metric.
selectionReasons.hybrid: A mixed-model or fallback configuration cannot represent one model’s capability.
selectionReasons.preRelease: The source explicitly identifies a prerelease version, which cannot represent an available released model.
selectionReasons.special: A specialized system or unverified run configuration cannot be attributed to one public model.
selectionReasons.tapTapContributor: The source’s contributor alias does not match a verified public model.
selectionReasons.terminalReferenceOnly: Retains complete model + Agent system scores for reference, without contributing to overall or coding ranks.

rowsNotes.systems: These are system scores for models paired with different Agents under different run conditions, for reference only. Up to 30 configurations are shown per benchmark. Anonymous test models are omitted.
rowsNotes.models: Fixed rules select one representative configuration per public model. Anonymous test models are omitted. Original source ranks are retained, with up to 30 models per benchmark.
